II. PROJECT DESCRIPTION
1. General
The subject of this statement is a proposed conventional urban renewal program (as previously described in part I) located in the city of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. The Department of Housing and Urban Development has designated it as Disaster Project R-634(c). Its official name is the Penn-Susquehanna Urban Renewal Project; however, for purposes of this report it will be referred to as "the project".
The project is being considered for final approval and funding by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) in an effort to offset the damage caused by Tropical Storm Agnes. Agnes struck the continental United States on June 19, 1972, and moved north causing heavy rainfall in Georgia and South Carolina. It proceeded up the East Coast through the Carolinas and caused heavy flooding along the Eastern Seaboard in Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey. After reaching the New Jersey Coast the storm turned west, on June 21 and June 22, and hit Pennsylvania full force. Due to a cold mass of air out of the West that caused the storm to stall over the Central and Northeastern parts of the State, and then moved back and forth over the same area, some of the worst flooding ever recorded in Pennsylvania occured during June 23-25, 1972.
In the Northeastern region of the Country at least 120,000 families suffered losses as a result of the Storm, and many public facilities were destroyed or temporarily knocked out. Most devestated was Pennsylvania with 31 deaths and over $1 billion in property damage.
On June 24th the Susquehanna River reached flood crest at 15 feet above flood level at Harrisburg and completely inundated the project area which lies within the 100-year flood plain (see appendix A, Approximate Flood Levels Map).
President Nixon declared the State of Pennsylvania a Federal disaster area on June 23, 1972, making the State eligible for certain special relief measures provided by the Federal Government. Shortly thereafter, Congress and the President set aside special funds to be used in the aid of flood victims and areas.
The proposed project will be funded with part of these special funds. Pennsylvania's total share of the funds amounted to $1.6 billion.
At this point in time the project application has passed through several critical stages (see Part IV, Decision Making Process)
